cases.concept_title: Virtual Memory and MMU Address Translation
cases.question_text: How does the hardware MMU translate virtual addresses into physical addresses, and what happens when a referenced virtual page is unmapped?
cases.ideal_answer_summary: The hardware MMU translates virtual page numbers into physical frame numbers using a page table. When a virtual page is unmapped, the MMU triggers a page fault trap to the OS kernel so the page can be loaded from disk into a physical frame.

required_ideas: MMU translates virtual page numbers into physical frame numbers using a page table
Unmapped virtual page triggers a page fault trap to the OS kernel to load the page from disk

criteria.name: MMU Virtual-to-Physical Translation
criteria.description: Explains virtual page number to physical frame translation via the page table.
required_ideas: MMU translates virtual page numbers into physical frame numbers using a page table

criteria.name: Page Fault Trap Handling
criteria.description: Explains that an unmapped page triggers a page fault trap to the OS kernel.
required_ideas: Unmapped virtual page triggers a page fault trap to the OS kernel to load the page from disk

cases.student_answer: The hardware MMU translates each process's virtual page numbers into physical frame numbers in RAM by consulting the page table. Because some pages reside on disk, referencing an unmapped virtual page causes the MMU to trigger a page fault trap to the OS kernel, which loads the required page from disk into a free physical frame.

cases.question_text: Calculate the Effective Access Time (EAT) in nanoseconds when TLB lookup takes 0 ns (overlapped), main memory access takes 100 ns, a TLB hit takes 1 memory access (100 ns), a TLB miss takes 2 memory accesses (200 ns), and the TLB hit ratio is 90% (0.90). Explain why a high hit ratio reduces EAT.
cases.ideal_answer_summary: The Effective Access Time equals 110 ns because 0.90 * 100 + 0.10 * 200 = 110 ns. A high TLB hit ratio avoids the extra main memory page table lookup on most translations.

required_ideas: Calculates Effective Access Time as 0.90 * 100 + 0.10 * 200 = 110 ns
Explains that TLB hits avoid the extra main memory page table lookup

criteria.name: TLB Hit vs Miss Explanation
criteria.description: Explains how TLB hits avoid walking the page table in main memory.
required_ideas: Explains that TLB hits avoid the extra main memory page table lookup

criteria.name: EAT Numerical Calculation
criteria.description: Correctly computes EAT = 110 ns.
required_ideas: Calculates Effective Access Time as 0.90 * 100 + 0.10 * 200 = 110 ns

cases.student_answer: Using the weighted average formula, EAT = 0.90 * 100 + 0.10 * 200 = 90 + 20 = 110 ns. Because 90% of translations hit in the TLB cache, the CPU avoids the extra main memory page table lookup on almost all accesses.

cases.concept_title: Raft Leader Election and Log Replication
cases.question_text: How does Raft elect a single leader and replicate client log entries safely across followers?
cases.ideal_answer_summary: Raft uses randomized election timeouts so a candidate requests votes via RequestVote RPCs and wins a majority quorum. The elected leader replicates log entries to followers using AppendEntries RPCs.

required_ideas: Randomized election timeouts and RequestVote RPCs require a majority quorum to elect a leader
Leader replicates client log entries to followers via AppendEntries RPCs

criteria.name: Leader Election & Majority Quorum
criteria.description: Explains randomized election timeouts, RequestVote RPCs, and majority quorum.
required_ideas: Randomized election timeouts and RequestVote RPCs require a majority quorum to elect a leader

criteria.name: AppendEntries Log Replication
criteria.description: Explains that the leader replicates log entries via AppendEntries RPCs.
required_ideas: Leader replicates client log entries to followers via AppendEntries RPCs

cases.student_answer: When followers time out using randomized election timeouts, a candidate increments its term and sends RequestVote RPCs, winning election once it secures a majority quorum of nodes. The elected leader then accepts client log entries and replicates them across followers via AppendEntries RPCs.

cases.question_text: What causes starvation in preemptive priority scheduling, and how does aging resolve it?
cases.ideal_answer_summary: Starvation occurs when a stream of high-priority processes indefinitely blocks low-priority processes from getting the CPU. Aging resolves starvation by gradually increasing the priority of processes that wait for a long time.

required_ideas: High-priority processes indefinitely block low-priority processes from CPU execution
Aging gradually increases the priority of waiting processes over time

required_ideas: Aging gradually increases the priority of waiting processes over time

cases.student_answer: Starvation happens because a continuous stream of high-priority processes keeps preempting the CPU so low-priority processes wait indefinitely in the ready queue.

cases.question_text: What role does the TLB play in address translation, and how do ASIDs affect context switches?
cases.ideal_answer_summary: The TLB is a fast hardware cache of recent virtual-to-physical translations; on a TLB miss the CPU walks the page table in main memory. ASIDs tag TLB entries by process to avoid flushing the entire TLB on every context switch.

required_ideas: TLB is a hardware cache of page table entries that walks main memory on a miss
ASIDs tag TLB entries by process to avoid flushing the entire TLB on context switches

criteria.name: TLB Cache Role
criteria.description: Explains TLB caching and page table walk on a miss.
required_ideas: TLB is a hardware cache of page table entries that walks main memory on a miss

criteria.name: ASID Context Switch Optimization
criteria.description: Explains how ASIDs prevent full TLB flushes.
required_ideas: ASIDs tag TLB entries by process to avoid flushing the entire TLB on context switches

cases.student_answer: The TLB completely replaces the page table in main memory so the TLB never misses, and ASIDs require flushing the entire TLB on every context switch.
cases.human_misconception: Claims the TLB completely replaces the page table in main memory or that TLB lookups never miss.
